title: Isolation patterns and evidence workbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This workbook records recommended VPC isolation patterns, firewall rule templates, mTLS deployment patterns, RBAC v2 mappings to network enforcement, and a practical evidence automation approach for Private Deployments. It is intended for engineers implementing customer private deployments and for compliance/SecOps teams collecting audit artifacts for attestations.

Summary of approach:
- Use layered isolation: network-level (VPC subnets + firewall policies), service-level (mTLS + mutual identity), and control-plane policies (RBAC v2).
- Tie RBAC role assertions into network enforcement via tag-based firewall rules and identity-derived access controls on the mTLS side.
- Generate a reproducible evidence bundle per deployment that includes: firewall rule diffs, signed mTLS certificate rotations, RBAC policy snapshots, and normalized audit log exports suitable for SIEM ingestion.

1) VPC isolation patterns (patterns are intentionally prescriptive)
- Minimal-hosting layout:
  - mgmt-subnet (private, bastion access via jump-host),
  - control-subnet (control plane nodes, API only from mgmt-subnet and customer VPC-peers),
  - compute-subnet (model serving nodes, no outbound internet except to artifact-repo endpoints),
  - egress-gateway-subnet (for controlled outbound and proxying).
- Peering and transit: prefer VPC peering with route controls or dedicated Transit Gateway equivalent; avoid broad 0.0.0.0/0 routes between customer and provider subnets.
- Flow logging: enable flow logs at subnet level and ship to centralized log bucket with object lifecycle and integrity checksums.

2) Firewall rule templates (canonical examples)
- Deny-all baseline: default deny ingress, allow only established session egress where necessary.
- Control-plane API rule (example):
  - source: mgmt-subnet-range OR customer-peered-subnet (CIDR),
  - dest: control-plane-api-ports 8443, 9443 (TLS),
  - protocol: TCP,
  - description: "control plane API - allow mgmt and peered VPCs"
- KV-cache and intra-cluster traffic:
  - allow only from compute-subnet ranges, TCP ports 11211, 6000-7000 (internal service range),
  - require mTLS at application layer (see section 3).
- Firewall rule tagging: attach RBAC role tags to firewall rules (see RBAC mapping).

3) mTLS and identity fabric
- Certificate authority model:
  - Use a short-lived leaf cert model: leaf certs rotated every 7 days by default, signed by an intermediate CA controlled by the deployment owner.
  - Use ACME-like automation or an internal CA signer with HSM-backed root stored off-line.
- Mutual auth flow:
  - Client and server present leaf certs; CN or SAN contains workload identity (format: service://<team>/<service>).
  - Validate against intermediate CA and check CRL/OCSP stapling.
- Authorization tie-in:
  - Enforce authorization beyond mTLS by mapping certificate identity to RBAC v2 roles (automated mapping service on ingress gateway).

4) RBAC v2 -> network enforcement mapping
- RBAC v2 model brief:
  - Principals: human or workload identities (OIDC sub claims or cert CN).
  - Roles: pre-defined roles (deployment-admin, network-ops, readonly-audit, model-deployer, support-agent).
  - Policies: fine-grained allow/deny on actions and resources.
- Mapping pattern:
  - Attach a "role-tag" attribute to the workload identity and to cloud network tags.
  - Firewall rule example: allow tcp:8443 from tag:role-model-deployer to control-plane-api only when the request carries a cert identity that maps to role-model-deployer. Implementation note: enforce at edge gateway/proxy that can inspect client cert and correlate with network tag.
- Policy snapshotting: export RBAC policies periodically (daily) in canonical JSON and include a SHA256 manifest in the evidence bundle.

5) Audit log schema (normalized JSON for SIEM)
- Naming goals: compact, deterministic fields, and cross-referencable IDs.
- Recommended fields (one-line field:type - example):
  - event_id:string - UUIDv4
  - timestamp:iso8601 - 2025-06-01T15:42:22Z
  - deploy_id:string - alphanumeric customer deployment id
  - host_ip:string - source IP or workload IP
  - src_identity:string - certificate CN / OIDC sub
  - src_role:string - resolved RBAC role
  - dst_service:string - logical dest (e.g., control-plane-api)
  - dst_port:integer - 8443
  - action:string - ALLOW|DENY|AUTH_FAIL|ROTATE_CERT
  - proto:string - TCP|UDP|HTTP|TLS
  - auth_result:string - success|failure|mfa_required
  - cert_serial:string - leaf cert serial (if present)
  - artifacts:string - list of artifact refs (S3 path, bundle id)
  - trace_id:string - correlates to request tracing
  - raw_log_link:string - pre-signed URL to raw event payload

Example audit record (compact JSON):
{
  "event_id": "9f8b7a6d-1234-4b2a-9c1e-0b1f2d3e4f5a",
  "timestamp": "2025-03-21T12:05:33Z",
  "deploy_id": "rwd-deploy-57",
  "host_ip": "10.2.5.12",
  "src_identity": "service://platform/gateway",
  "src_role": "network-ops",
  "dst_service": "control-plane-api",
  "dst_port": 8443,
  "action": "ALLOW",
  "proto": "TLS",
  "auth_result": "success",
  "cert_serial": "0A1B2C3D4E5F",
  "artifacts": "s3://rwd-evidence/rwd-deploy-57/fw-diff-20250321.json",
  "trace_id": "trace-abc-xyz",
  "raw_log_link": "https://logs.redwood.internal/pre-signed/abcd"
}

6) SIEM export formats and tips
- Preferred export: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) compressed with gzip, rotated hourly and pushed to SIEM ingestion endpoint. Include an index file with min/max timestamps and first/last event_id.
- Secondary: CEF for legacy SIEMs; map fields as follows: deviceVendor=Redwood, deviceProduct=PrivateDeploy, deviceEventClassID=event_id, name=action, severity=5; include src_identity in extension fields.
- Integrity: sign each export bundle manifest with deploy-owner signing key; include SHA256 checksums per file.

7) Evidence automation pipeline (opinionated recipe)
- Trigger points:
  - nightly scheduled run + on-config-change webhooks (firewall, RBAC, CA rotation).
- Steps per run:
  1. Pull current firewall rule set (cloud API) and compute a diff vs last committed ruleset.
  2. Dump RBAC policy snapshot (JSON) and compute SHA256.
  3. Export audit logs (NDJSON) for time window, normalize to audit schema, and compress.
  4. Capture certificate inventory (serials, not private keys) and rotation timestamps.
  5. Create a signed manifest.json that lists files, SHAs, timestamps, and signatures.
  6. Upload bundle to evidence bucket with deploy-specific prefix and set immutability policy (WORM) for retention period.
- Automation tips:
  - Use short-lived credentials for the automation runner and rotate them using a job managed by SRE.
  - Always redact PII before placing artifacts into long-lived buckets; keep a separate short-lived private bucket for full raw logs with stricter access controls.

8) Hardening checklist (operational)
- Pre-deployment:
  - [ ] Baseline deny-all firewall applied to subnets
  - [ ] Flow logs and VPC endpoint logging enabled
  - [ ] CA hierarchy provisioned and HSM root stored offline
  - [ ] RBAC v2 initial roles and policies reviewed by security
- During deployment:
  - [ ] mTLS enforced on all east-west and north-south gateways
  - [ ] Ingress gateway performs cert->role mapping and records decision in audit logs
  - [ ] Evidence automation job validated on staging and signing key available
- Post-deployment / continuous:
  - [ ] Daily RBAC snapshot exported, weekly policy review scheduled
  - [ ] Monthly certificate rotation drill completed and documented
  - [ ] SIEM ingest verified and alerts on missing expected bundles
  - [ ] Quarterly penetration test scope includes VPC peering and transit tests

9) Forensics and playbook snippets
- If unexpected egress observed:
  1. Immediately isolate suspect host by adding deny rule with high priority referencing host IP and tag it as quarantined.
  2. Trigger evidence automation for the last 72 hours with high-fidelity logs and preserve raw log bucket path.
  3. Generate an incident artifact bundle and assign incident id in manifest.

10) Diagrams (ASCII) - simplified topology:

  +-----------------+        +-----------------+        +-------------------+
  |  Customer VPC   | <----> |  Transit / Peer | <----> | Redwood Private   |
  |  (peered)       |        |  Gateway        |        |  VPC              |
  +-----------------+        +-----------------+        +-------------------+
                                                      | mgmt | control | compute |
                                                      +-------------------------------+
                                                      | egress-gw (mTLS enforced)    |
                                                      +-------------------------------+

Edge proxy (mTLS) sits in egress-gw; it verifies cert identity and resolves role_tag -> enforces firewall tag allowances and emits normalized audit records.

Appendix A: quick reference commands (cloud-agnostic pseudocode)
- Export firewall rules:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://cloud.api/v1/firewalls?filter=subnet=compute" > fw.json
- Compute diff against last:
  jq -S . fw.json > fw.sorted.json
  diff -u last-fw.sorted.json fw.sorted.json > fw-diff-$(date +%F).patch
- Create evidence bundle:
  tar -czf evidence-$(deploy)-$(date +%F).tgz fw.json rbacs.json audit.ndjson cert-inventory.json manifest.json
  aws s3 cp evidence-$(deploy)-$(date +%F).tgz s3://rwd-evidence/$(deploy)/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control

Appendix B: outstanding design considerations (open items)
- How to express conditional network allowances in RBAC policy language without duplicating rules across firewall and proxy.
- Best practice for certificate revocation at scale when many short-lived certs exist (OCSP scaling concerns).
- Mapping vendor SIEM field names to our canonical schema for easier cross-customer analysis.

Authors and review notes:
- Primary author: Maya Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- Reviewers: Carlos Liu (security), Anika Shah (SRE), Evan Brooks (platform)
- Next steps: prototype enforcement proxy that performs cert->role mapping and emits the normalized audit schema; demo on staging with one customer deployment.
